question: Find the domain of $\cos^{-1} \left( \frac{1}{x^3 - 3} \right)$.
explanation:
For $\cos^{-1}(u)$ to exist, the argument must satisfy $-1 \le u \le 1$.

Thus $-1 \le \frac{1}{x^3-3} \le 1$ and $x^3-3 \ne 0$.

Solving the inequality gives the conditions $x^3 \le 2$ or $x^3 \ge 4$.

Thus $x \le \sqrt[3]{2}$ or $x \ge \sqrt[3]{4}$.

Hence the domain is $(-\infty, \sqrt[3]{2}] \cup [\sqrt[3]{4}, \infty)$.
